objective: Put a measured price on a CFD-in-the-loop model search before anybody proposes one here, and state what fraction of the published search this lab's budget actually buys
rationale: Zhao et al. 2020, read in full 2026-08-02, is the one closure paper of the three this lab has read that states the cost of its expensive step: the CFD-driven training typically requires order ten to the three CPU hours, and section 4.2 names the mechanism, that candidate models iterate through hundreds or thousands of generations and every generation runs its CFD calculations. Converted at this lab's own measured rates, one thousand CPU hours is sixty thousand core-minutes, which is ninety wall-hours or 3.8 days of the entire box at 11.06 cores sustained under MPI, 13.8 days at the 3.02 busy mean, and 29.8 days at the 1.40 long-run mean. A per-evaluation cross-check grounds it in this lab's own instrument rather than the paper's: the turbine meshes are about 62,086 cells, 10.2 percent larger than the 56,320-cell bump rung measured here tonight at 0.63 seconds per iteration serial at 56,320 cells per rank, so a 200-step candidate evaluation is about 2.1 core-minutes and the published search is roughly 28,000 evaluations. The whole approved W1 queue after this week's triage is 647 core-minutes, which is 1.1 percent of one such search. The method is genuinely attractive here for a reason the cost does not touch, and that is why the price needs writing down first: the cost function needs only a mean-flow profile at two stations rather than dense per-cell Reynolds stresses, so it is the one method of the three that this lab's sparse experimental data could feed. The failure mode this item prevents is proposing it on the strength of that attraction and discovering the price afterwards, which is the same shape of error that put a 603 core-minute item and a 240 core-minute item in the approved queue this week.
gate: A costing note that states, from this lab's measured rates and cells per rank, the wall time and core-minutes of a CFD-driven search at the published scale, the number of candidate evaluations a stated budget buys, and the smallest search that could answer anything. Any future proposal for a CFD-in-the-loop search cites it or supersedes it with a better measurement
cost_basis: measured, and the measurement already exists. The rate is 0.63 seconds per iteration at 56,320 cells on one rank, read from the bump fine rung's own extension log on 2026-08-02, and the box rates of 1.40, 3.02 and 11.06 cores are the lab's standing figures. No solver run is needed to write the note
expected_knowledge_gain: A method whose cheapest published instance is between four days and a month of the entire box should be priced before it is wanted, not after
citations: Zhao, Akolekar, Weatheritt, Michelassi & Sandberg, RANS Turbulence Model Development using CFD-Driven Machine Learning, J. Comput. Phys. 2020, arXiv 1902.09075v2, sections 3.2 and 4.2, READ IN FULL 2026-08-02
The W2 CFD-driven training reading, sections 1 and 3
The W1 NASA bump grids record, section 4
in_sample_verdict: Not applicable, and it cannot become applicable. Nothing is fitted, inverted or calibrated: the deliverable is an arithmetic note over rates already measured. If a CFD-driven search is ever proposed here, the in-sample question arrives with it and not with this costing, and it will be sharp, because a cost function built on sparse mean-flow data is exactly the shape that tempts a lab toward the scored cases that ship experimental profiles.
